ideas.description: Trim the Muon knee by a quarter epoch. On the current tip (E023 commit 9c08ac0: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, SiLU, 7.0 epochs; or the I027/I028 successor if either is kept), change only the epoch count from 7.0 to 6.75. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E006/E018. The final partial batch must be a shape compiled in build(); add it to the warmup if it is new. Nothing else changes. If I027 or I028 is kept with a gain of 0.2 pp or more, use 6.5 epochs instead (one epoch-count change from that tip).
ideas.expected: At 6.75 epochs: accuracy 0.750-0.759, point ~0.7548 (tip 0.7568 minus ~0.8 pp/epoch x 0.25). Time 6.25-6.50 s, point ~6.33 s (-3.5%). Feasible means a new best with ~0.2 pp margin. If it is infeasible by less than 0.2 pp, keep the tip and retry after banking an lr, tail or averaging gain. The run also pins the Muon epoch slope below 7 epochs: a slope above 1.2 pp/epoch means the curve is steepening and further epoch cuts need recipe gains first.

ideas.description: Lengthen the lookahead averaging window on the Muon base. E020 shows averaging is worth ~0.9 pp with Muon, and the schedule (decay 0.95^5 x (t/T)^3, sync every 5 steps) was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10. On the current tip, change only the lookahead base decay from 0.95^5 (~0.774 per sync) to 0.97^5 (~0.859 per sync). That roughly doubles the effective averaging horizon late in training. The (t/T)^3 ramp, the sync interval of 5 steps, the final-weights handling and everything else stay unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp, point +0.1 pp (range 0.752-0.763 around tip 0.7568). Time unchanged within ±1.5%, since the blend has the same cost. A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.1 and buys ~0.25 epoch; then try 0.98^5 or a sync every 3 steps. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means the window is already long enough at this horizon; then test denser syncing (every 3 steps, same per-step decay) instead.

ideas.description: Combine the E011 near-miss with the epoch exchange rate. E011 priced block-3 width at ~0.13 pp per 1% of time, while cutting Muon epochs costs only ~0.056 pp per 1% (E022: 0.38 pp for 6.8%). So extra block-3 width paid for by fewer epochs should be a net win. On the current tip, widen only block 3 from 576 to 640 channels (a multiple of 64 for tensor-core tiling), keeping the head input and Muon groups consistent; the 640-wide filters stay batched as a same-shape pair in the compiled NS. Epochs stay at the tip's count. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first, and warm up the new shapes in build().
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.15 to +0.5 pp, point +0.3 pp. Time +3.5% to +6%, point +4.5% (~6.85 s at 7 epochs; block 3 is ~25% of step time per E011, and the NS cost grows a little). Not a new best by itself. A gain of 0.3 pp or more for 5% time or less beats the epoch rate, so follow up with 640 width at 6.5 epochs (net ~-2.5% time at equal accuracy). A gain under 0.15 pp means width returns have saturated at 576 under Muon; then close the width branch.

ideas.description: Muon's updates have a fixed magnitude (an orthogonalized step against a weight-norm projection), so the SGD-style warmup (23% of steps ramping from 0.2x) may waste early steps for the conv filters. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier during warmup: hold it at 1.0x from step 0, and keep the existing decay shape and floor after the warmup point. The SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) keeps its full warmup schedule. Lookahead, NS3, momentum and epochs are unchanged. Check finite gradients for the first ~20 steps on synthetic data in drafts/ before launching.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp. Time unchanged within ±1.5%. A gain of 0.25 pp or more means early steps are under-used at 7 epochs and buys ~0.3 epoch; then shorten the SGD-group warmup as a separate run. A loss of 0.25 pp or more (early instability with BN at full rotation size) closes the warmup axis for Muon. This is distinct from E012, which bundled a warmup cut with decay-to-zero for all params under SGD.

ideas.description: Systems change to the conv shapes, with the learning recipe unchanged. First, in drafts/, print the activation spatial sizes per block and run a per-layer profile of the tip (untimed, not an experiment). If the unpadded 2x2 whitening conv outputs 31x31, block 1's first conv runs at 31x31, and max-pool(2) then floors that to 15x15, so its last row and column are computed and discarded. Make one change: slice the whitening output to [..., :30, :30] in the model's forward, identically in train and eval. This is a fixed architecture step, not TTA, and eval still accepts 32x32 inputs for any B. Every downstream pooled shape is unchanged (15/7/3); the only math change is that row and column 29 see zero padding instead of row and column 30. Warm up the new shapes in build() and run the finite-gradient check. If the profile shows the net already runs at even sizes (32/16/8/4), skip this idea and mark H2.5.2 not applicable.
ideas.expected: Time -1% to -4%, point -2% (~6.43 s): ~6.5% fewer FLOPs and memory traffic in block 1's first conv and its BN/SiLU, plus any gain from even-sized tiles. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp (re-draw only). A gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1 and closes conv-shape work. A gain of 3% or more supports H2.5.2.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E023: Muon NS3, batched and compiled, at 7.0 epochs, scoring 0.7568 in 6.56 s with a 0.38 pp margin over the 0.753 bar. I027 (Muon lr 0.16) is running. Three ideas are queued: I028 (Muon lr floor to 0), I029 (momentum 0.8) and I030 (frequency-split Muon). All their hypotheses are still open, so I dropped none.

I added five ideas, which brings the queue to 8:
1. **Epoch cut to 6.75** (priority 4, exploit, H1.2.1): about -3.5% time, landing near 0.7548. If I027 or I028 bank a gain of 0.2 pp or more, the cut becomes 6.5 epochs instead.
2. **Longer lookahead window** (priority 3, exploit, H1.6.1): decay 0.95^5 → 0.97^5, since averaging is worth about 0.9 pp on Muon (E020).
3. **Block-3 width 576 → 640** (priority 3, exploit, H1.5.1): combines the E011 near-miss with the exchange rates. Width is priced at about 0.13 pp per 1% of time, while Muon epochs cost about 0.056 pp per 1%. So extra width paid for with fewer epochs should be a net win.
4. **No warmup for the Muon group** (priority 2, explore, H1.2): Muon's updates have a fixed size, so the warmup may waste early steps.
5. **Slice the whitening output to 30x30** (priority 2, explore, H2.5.2): if the profile confirms the shapes, this removes the conv row and column that max-pool on 31x31 discards. It is gated on that per-layer profile.

I left out NorMuon/PolarAdamW. With wide flattened filters and a weight-norm projection, the rows are already near-uniform, so that change should do nothing (the same reasoning D006 gave for skipping Aurora). I also left out batch-size and hard-example selection: at about 7 epochs, they cost per-epoch sample efficiency.
